hazard: Communication failures to London Ambulance Service
theme: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

reports.title: Edir DA Costa
categories: Alcohol, drug and medication related deaths

promises.quote: request that the working group, driven by Met training, review the attendance of officers at mandatory ELS training and review the systems in place for supervisors to monitor attendance
promises.summary: review training attendance and improve monitoring systems

promises.quote: The MPS are requested to review the training provided to staff in relation to the role of the safety officer in a street setting and to consider whether a reminder of the importance of the safety officer role, in the street setting, should be issued to staff (by way of bulletin or otherwise)
promises.summary: review safety officer role training and issue reminder

promises.quote: Future restraint lessons will reference the revised Module 12 of the National Personal Safety Manual (NPSM) which was presented by Inspector Collett during the Inquest as the final draft
promises.summary: update restraint training to include choking risk guidance

promises.quote: The MPS is requested to review the guidance and procedures in place for officers, in relation to the use of CS spray where a person is believed to be holding items in their mouth
promises.summary: review CS spray procedures with mouth contents

concerns.quote: not all police officers are up to date with mandatory Emergency Life Support training
concerns.hazard: lack of mandatory Emergency Life Support training among police officers

concerns.quote: safety officer had taken control of the restraint or that one officer was taking the lead in communicating with Mr Da Costa and/or monitoring his condition
concerns.hazard: absence of designated safety officer oversight in street restraint

concerns.quote: Placing plastic bags in the mouth raises a very high risk of choking.
concerns.hazard: high choking risk from plastic bags placed in mouth

concerns.quote: use of CS spray, when a person has something in their mouth, could increase the risk of a complete airway obstruction
concerns.hazard: CS spray use with mouth contents increasing airway obstruction risk

concerns.quote: agonal breaths were likely to have been missed
concerns.hazard: missed recognition of agonal breaths by officers

concerns.quote: errors were made in communicating information to the LAS
concerns.hazard: communication failures to London Ambulance Service

promises.quote: The MPS will shortly be introducing a Merlin Toolkit, which will provide advice and guidance on the circumstances in which reports should be completed. This also references the Vulnerability Assessment Framework (VAF) which should be used as the basis for assessment for all officers.
promises.summary: Introduce Merlin Toolkit to guide officers on when to complete Merlin Reports

links.explanation: Both reports highlight failures by police to convey critical health‑related information to medical responders. The earlier report cites communication breakdowns with the London Ambulance Service due to noise and procedural lapses; the later report describes police not passing on vital patient statements and observations to ambulance crews and hospital staff.
links.earlier_quote: Evidence was heard at the Inquest that errors were made in communicating information to the LAS.
links.later_quote: The police officer did not pass on this crucial account to the emergency ambulance crew who transported Ms Marchessou to hospital, nor to any of the doctors or nurses at the hospital.
